module_notes.note: lib/device/snmpdevice.py is the SNMP base class every switch and AP inherits, so any defect here is fleet-wide. The module is broadly careful (None-on-failure contract is documented, disk cache deliberately refuses to persist None), but it has two real high-blast-radius defects that prior passes missed because they treated this file as context. (1) The shared cached_property/disk_cached_property decorators cache a *failed* SNMP read for the entire process (cached_property) or across runs (disk_cached_property) — None and empty-string are both poisoning values that never refresh, so one transient SNMP miss freezes a device's firmware/config/serial for the rest of the run and feeds stale values into report/validate/update. (2) generic_get returns an empty string '' (not None) on the walk-prefer failure path, and device_stats only guards against None — so memory_total/memory_free of '' crashes telemetry for the Westermo AP brand (the one brand with snmp_prefer_walk=True) with a TypeError. The SNMP engine singleton is shared across all device instances; this version dodges the concurrency bug by having removed the telemetry ThreadPool (confirmed in backbone_telemetry.py comment), but the singleton + per-instance engine reset in _wait_for_snmp is a latent footgun if threads are ever reintroduced. Secondary: _inject_metadata hard-subscripts cfg['train_id']/cfg['project_id'] which raises KeyError on an incompletely-configured CCU during config render.

walker.py is the base discovery class shared by LldpWalker and LldpArpWalker — instantiate_device() runs for EVERY device on EVERY discover across the whole fleet, and is_new_mac/is_new_ip gate which devices survive the walk. The factory/dispatch path (brand lookup → class existence check → instantiation) is actually sound: find_brand() only ever returns brands present in vendor_specific, the None case is handled, missing-class and non-existent-class are guarded, and the one constructor that does SNMP at init time (vsc7429) raises only SNMPDeviceException, which walker catches — so a single unreachable device degrades gracefully rather than aborting the whole walk. build_ccu_device() is also reasonable (LLDP failure on one interface is ERROR-not-fatal; empty result is CRITICAL-logged). The real defects are in the de-duplication gate, which both subclasses copy verbatim: `if self.is_new_mac(mac) and self.is_new_ip(ip):`. Both methods MUTATE state, and Python `and` short-circuits — so (a) a genuinely new device whose IP collides with an already-seen device is silently dropped, and (b) when the MAC short-circuits to False the IP is never registered, corrupting found_ip_addresses. The shared-IP drop directly contradicts a documented field reality (ZFR / Sprechstelle redundancy pairs intentionally share one IP), so the redundant partner vanishes from the consist on every discover. There are no unit tests covering is_new_mac/is_new_ip purity or the shared-IP case.

decorators.py is the platform-wide caching layer wrapping device SNMP properties (serial_number, firmware/config version via the @cached_property hierarchy, plus memory_total, port_mtu/name/type via @disk_cached_property) across every vendor driver and every device on every train. Three real defects, in descending blast radius: (1) the disk cache is a silent fleet-wide no-op because its default db path /tmp/obn/shelve lives in a directory no code ever creates and shelve flag 'c' cannot create a missing parent dir — confirmed by the project's own test_disk_cached_property__failed which codifies the failure; (2) the disk cache key derives from obj.mac which defaults to '00:00:00:00:00:00' in SNMPDevice.__init__, so any device constructed without a real MAC collides in the cache namespace (one device's serial/firmware served to another) — latent today because of defect 1, but goes live the moment /tmp/obn exists or the path is fixed; (3) _save_to_disk_cache only refuses to persist None, but the SNMP read paths it wraps also yield '' (generic_get walk-miss returns '' for any cast, including the int casts in memory_total) — an empty-string is an equally-failed retrieval that the docstring's own reasoning says should not be cached, yet it gets persisted permanently and served on every later read/run. ip_lookup.py and the helpers in __init__.py are comparatively solid; ARPLookup uses a class-level cached dict (shared mutable state) but OBN walkers are not described as multithreaded here so I did not raise it as a concurrency defect. Net: the central caching feature this module exists to provide is effectively dead in production, and the two correctness traps (key collision, empty-string poisoning) are armed and would bite immediately if the dead-cache bug were 'fixed' without addressing them.

`obn validate` is a commissioning gate run on every train, and the validate module has multiple false-OK paths. The most serious is structural: backbone_validate.validate() (the function the `obn validate` CLI command invokes) calls val.run_all(), prints any failures to stderr, and then RETURNS NORMALLY — it never raises and never sys.exit()s on NOK/CRITICAL results. So the `obn validate` shell command exits 0 even on a fully broken consist; any wrapper/CI/commissioning script keying off exit code sees PASS. Secondly, the TGV subclass (TGV2020Validate) adds the only real topology/coach-count/media checks, but (a) backbone_validate.validate() always instantiates the base Validate(), never the TGV subclass, and (b) run_all()'s static all_validations list does not include the TGV test names, so those checks never run through `obn validate` regardless. The base test suite itself only checks file-exists / non-empty / any-devices / key-presence / mac-coverage — it has no positive structural assertion (expected device count, one switch per coach, no duplicate coach numbers), so a consist that discovers a wrong/short device set but with complete per-device keys validates as OK. The narrow per-device checks also have None-value and missing-key gaps. This central gate is NOT solid; a broken train can be signed off.

This module derives CCU/box identity that roots every report's coach numbering (coach-0/box detection) and the CCU's own IP/MAC/serial/version. The highest-blast-radius issues are in lib/context.py CCUContext, which (a) reads cfg["train_type"] with a bracket access that KeyErrors the whole report when the key is absent, and (b) silently falls back to coach number 1 for any box it can't map — a misnumbering of the entire consist with no warning. Combined with CCUContext being a process-global singleton (class attributes guarded by _initialized, never refreshed except via reset() for tests), a wrong identity computed once poisons every subsequent report in a long-running OBN process. ccudevice.py is comparatively careful (ioctl OSError suppressed, file-existence guards), but CCUDevice.ip is computed from config arithmetic with no validation and CCUDevice.mac caches an "unknown" sentinel for the whole process. nomad_ccu.py creates a process-global SnmpEngine singleton with no locking, shared across the telemetry scheduler.

obn.py command routing is largely sound: @requires_root gates every stateful command, the report dispatch (obn.py:82-90) correctly checks hasattr before getattr and exits 1 on a bad report_module, and the exception hook logs unhandled exceptions as CRITICAL. The one genuinely high-blast-radius defect in this module's scope lives in the telemetry path (backbone_telemetry.py, dispatched from obn.py:114-126): the per-device loop dereferences the result of instantiate_device() with no None guard, even though that function has three documented `return None` exits. The telemetry test for that path is an empty `pass` stub, confirming the GenericReport-style blind spot. Two lower-severity observations: (1) the telemetry scheduler uses APScheduler interval defaults with no max_instances/misfire/coalesce tuning, so a slow SNMP cycle that overruns the interval is silently dropped by the default max_instances=1; (2) NOTE the VERSION constant in obn.py is "2.2.6", not the "2.3.12" named in the audit brief — the checked-out tree may not be the version stated, worth confirming the right ref was reviewed. Configuration singleton init order (obn.py __main__ builds it then passes obj=, while cli() also ensure_object) is benign because the class-level _config cache makes the second construction a no-op.

confirmed.title: Disk cache is a silent fleet-wide no-op: default db dir /tmp/obn is never created
confirmed.blast_radius: all SNMP devices on all trains
confirmed.claim: disk_cached_property defaults db to '/tmp/obn/shelve'. _retrieve_from_disk_cache opens with flag 'c' when the path is absent (line 57-58), but shelve/dbm 'c' cannot create a db inside a non-existent parent directory, and nothing in the OBN tree ever creates /tmp/obn (grep for makedirs/mkdir/'/tmp/obn' shows only unrelated tftp/firmware dirs). The resulting dbm.error is caught and logged as a mere warning at line 60-62, and _save_to_disk_cache hits the same failure at line 81. So every @disk_cached_property (serial_number, memory_total, port_mtu, port_name, port_type, and the disk-cached props in westermo/extreme/acksys/tipg541/tng4500/eltec_cybox/vsc7429) falls back to live SNMP every time and never persists across runs or reboots. The project's own test_disk_cached_property__failed (tests/lib/util/test_decorators.py:130) asserts 'failed to open disk cache' as expected behavior, confirming the path never works in default config. Verified locally: shelve.open('/tmp/obnnest/shelve', flag='c') with a missing parent raises dbm.error FileNotFoundError.
confirmed.trigger: Any OBN run on any CCU where /tmp/obn does not already exist (i.e. all of them at process start) — every disk-cached property quietly degrades to live SNMP, the disk cache's entire purpose is defeated.

verdict.reasoning: Statically provable. decorators.py:48 defaults db="/tmp/obn/shelve". _retrieve_from_disk_cache (lines 53-64) opens shelve with flag 'c' when the path is absent; _save_to_disk_cache (66-82) opens flag 'w'. Both wrap shelve.open in `except dbm.error` -> logger.warning, and __get__ (101-105) falls back to the live function when retrieval returns _missing. shelve/dbm cannot create a db inside a non-existent parent dir: I reproduced shelve.open(<missing-parent>/shelve, flag='c') -> FileNotFoundError/dbm.error locally. No upstream guard exists: grep over the whole OBN tree shows /tmp/obn/shelve appears ONLY at the default-arg site; no makedirs/mkdir ever creates /tmp/obn (the only makedirs/mkdir calls -- snmpdevice.py:543/567, update.py:167, acksys.py:582 -- build TFTP config/firmware folders). No caller overrides db= (all 16 decorated sites in snmpdevice.py and vendor/*.py use the bare decorator). So on any CCU where /tmp/obn does not pre-exist at process start, every @disk_cached_property silently falls back to live SNMP and never persists across runs/reboots. NOT a duplicate of the snmp None-return finding -- this is the disk-cache directory bug, an independent root cause. Severity downgraded: this is a performance/efficiency degradation, not a correctness fault. Within a single process the in-memory cached_property layer (line 109 writes to obj.__dict__) still dedupes each property to one SNMP fetch per device; the failure is caught and the correct live value is returned. Impact = lost cross-run/cross-reboot SNMP-avoidance optimization plus a benign warning log, not any functional break. Blast-radius wording 'all SNMP devices on all trains' is accurate in scope but the consequence is extra SNMP round-trips, not data loss or failure.
verdict.covered_by_test: tests/lib/util/test_decorators.py:130 test_disk_cached_property__failed -- a green test that exercises the bare default decorator (db="/tmp/obn/shelve") and asserts BOTH that the property still returns its live value (1) AND that 'failed to open disk cache' appears in the warning log. This test codifies the no-op as expected behavior, i.e. it confirms (does not refute) the claim. All other disk-cache tests override db= via tmp_path, so none assert the default path works or that /tmp/obn is ever created.
verdict.blast_radius_adjusted: Fleet-wide in scope (every @disk_cached_property on every SNMPDevice -- serial_number, memory_total, port_mtu/name/type in snmpdevice.py plus vendor variants in westermo/extreme/acksys/tipg541/tng4500/eltec_cybox/vsc7429 -- on every CCU/train at process start when /tmp/obn is absent). Effect is the disk cache silently never persisting across runs/reboots, so those properties re-fetch via live SNMP each run. No correctness impact: single-run in-memory caching still holds and the live value is returned; the only cost is redundant SNMP round-trips plus a 'failed to open disk cache' warning per affected property.

confirmed.title: obn validate always exits 0 — run_all() failures never propagate to exit code
confirmed.claim: backbone_validate.validate() calls val.run_all() (line 146), iterates results printing '⚠ {test}: {result}' to stderr (lines 147-148), then continues to print the device tables and returns None. It never raises and never calls sys.exit() based on the validation results. The obn.py `validate` CLI command (obn.py:104-108) just calls bb_validate and returns. Therefore `obn validate` returns shell exit code 0 even when run_all() recorded NOK or CRITICAL failures (no devices discovered, empty/missing discovery.json once tables fall through, incomplete devices, unnumbered devices). A commissioning script, CI step, or orchestrator gate that checks `obn validate` exit status sees success on a broken consist.
confirmed.trigger: Run `obn validate` on a train with validation failures (e.g. unnumbered or incomplete devices); the warnings print to stderr but `echo $?` is 0.

verdict.reasoning:
Statically provable from the cited code. backbone_validate.validate() (src/usr/share/obn/backbone_validate.py:140-182) calls val.run_all() (line 146), prints each result to stderr as a warning (lines 147-148), then prints device tables and returns None. It never inspects the recorded Severity (Severity.NOK / Severity.CRITICAL defined in lib/validate/validate.py:11-15), never re-raises ValidationError, and never calls sys.exit() based on validation results. The CLI command obn.py:104-108 simply calls bb_validate(...) and returns; a normally-returning Click command exits 0. Therefore NOK failures (test_incomplete_devices line 192-195, test_unnumbered_devices line 213-216) and the CRITICAL 'no devices' failure (test_any_devices line 136-154, which yields an empty-but-present report list so tables still render) all leave the process exit code at 0 — exactly as the claim states.

One honest correction to the claim's scope: load_devices() (backbone_validate.py:130-137) DOES sys.exit(1) when cfg.report_file is missing. So the specific sub-case 'missing/empty discovery.json once tables fall through' and the missing-report-file CRITICAL case actually exit 1 — but by an incidental file-existence check in the table phase, not by run_all() propagating severity. The masking is genuine for incomplete devices, unnumbered devices, and empty-device-list cases where the report file exists. The central mechanism the claim describes (run_all failures never propagating to exit code) is correct.
verdict.covered_by_test: No covering/refuting test. tests/lib/validate/test_validate.py (lines 39-92) asserts only the CONTENTS of the dict returned by run_all() (e.g. assert results == {...}); it never asserts a process exit code for `obn validate` and never asserts that failures propagate to a non-zero status. tests/test_backbone_validate.py exercises only the Table rendering class (imports Table, line 6), not the validate() entrypoint or its exit behavior. Nothing green asserts the opposite of the claim.
verdict.blast_radius_adjusted: Code-wise it is the single validate path, so it affects `obn validate` on every train. But realistic impact is narrow: within the allowed scope I found no consumer (script/CI/orchestrator gate) that branches on `obn validate`'s exit code. The documented OBN workflow and skill docs treat `obn validate` as human-readable diagnostic table output (discover → report → validate, read visually), not a pass/fail gate. So the 'broken consist silently passes a gate' harm requires an exit-code-checking caller that does not appear to exist today. Stated blast 'all trains' is technically true for the behavior but overstated for actual impact — effectively dormant unless someone wires validate into automation.

confirmed.title: TGV topology/coach/media checks never execute via obn validate (subclass unused + not registered)
confirmed.claim: run_all()'s all_validations static list (validate.py:47-54) contains only the six base tests; the comment at lines 42-46 says any new validation must be added to this list to run. TGV2020Validate (validate_tgv2020.py) defines test_nrof_coaches, test_media_location and test_topology — the only checks that assert real structure (expected coach count, exactly one switch and two APs per coach, no UNKNOWN devices, media-box placement) — but none of these names appear in all_validations, and TGV2020Validate does not override run_all to add them. Compounding this, backbone_validate.validate() (backbone_validate.py:145) hardcodes the base `Validate()` and never instantiates TGV2020Validate. Net effect: the structural validations are dead code from the `obn validate` entrypoint. A consist with a missing switch, an extra/unknown device, or wrong coach count passes validation.
confirmed.trigger: Run `obn validate` on any consist with a missing/extra backbone device; the per-coach SW==1 / AP==2 / UNKNOWN==0 assertions never fire.

verdict.reasoning: Statically provable as a dead-code wiring gap. (1) run_all() at validate.py:41-71 iterates a static all_validations list (lines 47-54) containing only the six base tests: test_discovery_json, test_report_json_exists, test_any_devices, test_mac_address_file_exists, test_incomplete_devices, test_unnumbered_devices. The comment at 42-46 confirms a new validation MUST be added to this list to run. (2) I read the entire TGV2020Validate subclass (validate_tgv2020.py:1-67): it defines only test_nrof_coaches, test_media_location, test_topology and does NOT override run_all — so even if instantiated, run_all would still run only the six base names (the three TGV names are never in the list). (3) backbone_validate.validate() hardcodes `val = Validate()` at backbone_validate.py:145 and calls val.run_all() at 146; this is the only run_all caller in src. (4) grep over the whole src tree shows TGV2020Validate is referenced only at its own definition and the lib/validate/__init__.py re-export — it is never instantiated anywhere. obn.py:104-108 (`obn validate`) calls backbone_validate.validate, which uses the base class. There is no train-type-based subclass selection in the validate layer (unlike the report layer, which selects TGV2020Report/report_dosto_neu/etc. by train_type). Net: via `obn validate`, the structural TGV checks (coach count, 1 SW + 2 AP per coach, no UNKNOWN, media-box placement) never execute. No upstream guard routes to the subclass. CORRECTION to the claim's framing: these are TGV2020-fleet checks (docstring: "only applicable to TGV topologies"; expects 7/8/9 coaches and exactly 3 media boxes) — that model does not apply to the DOSTO NEU fleet this project targets, so "all trains" is wrong; and the base six tests still run, only the deeper structural checks are skipped.
verdict.covered_by_test: Not covered for the wiring gap. tests/lib/validate/test_validate_tgv2020.py exercises the three TGV methods, but it calls them DIRECTLY on a hand-built TGV2020Validate() instance (val.test_topology(), val.test_nrof_coaches(), val.test_media_location()) — it never goes through run_all() or backbone_validate.validate(), so it does not assert the checks are reachable from the obn validate entrypoint. tests/test_backbone_validate.py only tests the Table rendering class (Table._validate / create_*_overview), never the Validate()/run_all() wiring in backbone_validate.validate(). No test asserts the opposite (no green test proving TGV checks run via the CLI), so the finding is not refuted by tests; the entrypoint wiring is uncovered.
verdict.blast_radius_adjusted: TGV2020 fleet only (the subclass is explicitly TGV-topology-specific: 7/8/9 coaches, 3 media boxes). NOT platform-wide and NOT applicable to the DOSTO NEU fleet, which uses report_dosto_neu and a different consist model. Even on TGV2020, the six base validate tests still run via run_all(); only the deeper structural assertions (per-coach SW==1/AP==2/UNKNOWN==0, coach-count, media placement) are skipped. `obn validate` is a read-only operator sanity/overview command, not a gate guarding any destructive push — so a malformed consist passes a sanity print but does not trigger a misconfiguration. "all trains" / high-blast-radius in the original claim is overstated.

confirmed.title: No positive structural assertion — non-empty but wrong/short device list reads as healthy
confirmed.claim: The base validations only check: discovery.json exists/non-empty (test_discovery_json), report file exists (test_report_json_exists), len(devices) > 0 (test_any_devices, lines 136-154), per-device key presence (test_incomplete_devices), and discovered-vs-reported MAC coverage (test_unnumbered_devices). There is no check that the device COUNT matches the expected consist size, no check for duplicate coach/device numbers, and no per-coach role check (since the TGV structural tests don't run — see separate finding). A consist that discovers only a fraction of its switches/APs but where every discovered device has complete keys and a coach number passes all base validations. all([]) is not the trigger here; the gap is that 'some devices, all well-formed' is accepted as 'the train is correctly built'. This is the GenericReport blind-spot pattern: the gate confirms data shape, not consist correctness.
confirmed.trigger: Half a consist offline during discovery; the discovered subset all has complete keys and coach numbers → obn validate reports OK.

verdict.reasoning: Statically provable. backbone_validate.validate() (the `obn validate` entrypoint, obn.py:106 → backbone_validate.py:140) hardcodes `val = Validate()` at line 145 — the base class. The base run_all() (validate.py:47-54) executes exactly six tests: test_discovery_json (file exists/non-empty), test_report_json_exists (file exists), test_any_devices (len>0 for discovered AND reported, lines 136-154), test_mac_address_file_exists, test_incomplete_devices (required-key subset check), test_unnumbered_devices (discovered-MAC ⊆ reported-MAC). NONE asserts device count vs expected consist size, duplicate coach/device numbers, or per-coach role counts. The structural assertions (test_topology, test_nrof_coaches, test_media_location) live ONLY in TGV2020Validate (validate_tgv2020.py); that subclass is imported in lib/validate/__init__.py but is NEVER instantiated by the production entrypoint — backbone_validate always uses base Validate. For DOSTO-NEU there is no validate subclass at all. Trigger confirmed: a partial consist (e.g. 5 of 18 switches discovered) where every discovered device has complete keys and a coach number passes all six tests. test_unnumbered_devices does NOT catch it because an offline switch is absent from BOTH discovered and reported lists (it compares the two lists, not against an expected manifest). The claim correctly distinguishes itself from the known all([]) update-c no-op: here it's `some-but-wrong devices` accepted as healthy. No upstream guard: report_dosto_neu.number_coaches() does coach numbering and normalise_devices() only DROPS mis-detected devices — it never asserts a full consist. NOT a duplicate of the snmp-None-return finding (different module, different failure mode).
verdict.covered_by_test: Not covered for the production path. tests/lib/validate/test_validate.py has NO test asserting a short non-empty list fails — test_run_all__any_devices_none_discovered (lines 56-64) only triggers on `[]`, and test_run_all__any_devices_none_reported only on empty reported list. The structural tests in tests/lib/validate/test_validate_tgv2020.py (test_test_topology, test_test_topology_fail_sw, etc.) exercise TGV2020Validate directly and assert the opposite (they DO catch a missing switch) — but they cover the unused subclass, not the base Validate that `obn validate` actually runs, so they provide no coverage for the gap and confirm the structural check exists only in the TGV branch.
verdict.blast_radius_adjusted: Narrower than 'all trains' as a critical risk. obn validate is a read-only human-facing diagnostic (prints a device table); it does NOT gate any destructive operation. Commissioning safety relies on dosto-device-discovery (per CLAUDE.md) which independently checks the expected device count (12+16 nv4 / 18+24 nv6) and pinpoints missing devices — that external gate partially compensates. The real harm is a false reassurance for an engineer who reads `obn validate` output alone. Affects every train type routed through base Validate (all non-TGV, including all ÖBB DOSTO-NEU consists); TGV-class trains would be covered IF the subclass were wired in, but it isn't, so even they only get base coverage via the entrypoint.

confirmed.title: test_incomplete_devices accepts present-but-None SNMP fields (issubset checks keys only)
confirmed.claim: test_incomplete_devices flags a device only when `not required_keys.issubset(device)` (lines 186-191). issubset against a dict tests key membership, so a device dict that contains keys 'firmware','config','serial','uptime' etc. with value None (the common shape when an SNMP get failed or returned nothing) is treated as COMPLETE. The required-keys set therefore validates devices whose SNMP-derived fields are null. A switch/AP that responded to discovery but whose firmware/config/serial could not be read (transient SNMP failure, factory-config AP silently dropping SNMP per the known fleet quirk) passes the completeness gate.
confirmed.trigger: A device row with {'mac':..,'ip':..,'serial':None,'firmware':None,'config':None,'uptime':None,'neighbours':[]} — issubset is True, no ValidationError raised.

verdict.reasoning: Cited code (validate.py:186-191) verified verbatim: `not required_keys.issubset(device)`. A dict iterates over keys, so issubset tests key NAMES only, never values. The None values genuinely arise and reach this gate: SNMP failure -> _snmp_parse_results returns {} (snmpdevice.py:288-292) -> _snmp_get returns None (line 340); serial_number/firmware_version/configuration_version all `return snmp` unchanged -> None (lines 200,228,236). Device.as_dict() (device.py:12-21) UNCONDITIONALLY emits all 7 required keys regardless of value, and report.py serializes that to report_file via dump_device_instances->json.dump (lines 50,138-141) with no None-filtering anywhere in the path. Therefore a device that answered discovery (MAC/IP) but failed SNMP serial/firmware/config reads is written as {serial:null,firmware:null,config:null,...} with all keys present -> issubset True -> test_incomplete_devices raises nothing. No upstream guard checks the values. Statically provable from the code alone. NOTE: the stated CLASS 'none_deref' is wrong - there is NO NoneType dereference and no crash; test_incomplete_devices is itself None-safe. This is a weak-assertion / silent-false-negative logic bug: the validator marks an SNMP-incomplete device as complete. Confirmed as a real defect, but the failure mode is 'validation passes a device it should flag', not a crash.
verdict.covered_by_test: tests/lib/validate/test_validate.py::TestValidate::test_test_incomplete_devices (lines 16-25) exists but does NOT cover the present-but-None case. It supplies a device with only {mac, ip} (the other 5 keys ABSENT) and asserts ValidationError is raised - exercising the missing-key path only. A device with all 7 keys present and null values would silently pass, and this test would still be green. So the bug is NOT covered/refuted by any test; the existing test actually confirms issubset is the (key-only) mechanism.
verdict.blast_radius_adjusted: Narrower than the stated 'all SNMP devices'. Scope = the `obn validate` completeness-reporting path only (backbone_validate.py -> Validate.run_all -> test_incomplete_devices). Not a crash, not a runtime deref, no impact on discover/report/update flows. Manifests only when a device responds to discovery but its SNMP serial/firmware/config reads return None (transient SNMP failure, or factory-config AP silently dropping SNMP - both documented real fleet conditions). Effect is a false-negative: `obn validate` reports such a device as complete/healthy instead of flagging incomplete info. Cosmetic/diagnostic-quality impact, condition-dependent, no functional or safety consequence downstream.

confirmed.title: CCUContext silently defaults unknown box to coach number 1, misnumbering the whole consist
confirmed.claim: In the multi-CCU branch, when box_coach_numbers is defined but neither the train_type-specific map nor the 'default' map contains this CCU's box id, coach_number falls back to the literal default 1 via topology['box_coach_numbers'].get('default', {}).get(CCUContext._ccu_box_id, 1). There is no warning and no failure. Because CCUContext.get_current_ccu_coach_number() roots number_coaches()/coach-0 assignment in report_generic.py and report.py, a wrong or unrecognised box id silently numbers the CCU's coach as 1 and offsets/mislabels every downstream coach in the consist. A misimaged CCU (wrong hostname → wrong box id via socket.getfqdn() at line 29) lands here and produces a plausible-but-wrong report rather than an error.
confirmed.trigger: Multi-CCU train (box_coach_numbers present in topology) where the running CCU's box id is not a key in either the train_type map or the 'default' map — e.g. misimaged CCU with an unexpected FQDN, or a topology YAML missing this box's entry.

verdict.reasoning: Cited code is exact. context.py:41-45 (multi-CCU branch) computes coach_number = topology["box_coach_numbers"].get("default", {}).get(CCUContext._ccu_box_id, 1). When box_coach_numbers exists but the running CCU's box id is in neither the train_type map (lines 33-38) nor the 'default' map, the dict.get default returns the literal 1. verdict.covered_by_test: No covering test. tests/test_backbone_telemetry.py only tests message formatting (test_create_device_stats_message, test_create_port_stats_messages); test_telemetry_device is an empty "pass" stub with a TODO. grep across tests/ for scheduler/add_job/apscheduler/max_instances/misfire matched only the message-format file. No test exercises the scheduler config or overrun behavior, and none asserts the opposite.
verdict.blast_radius_adjusted: Narrower than the stated "all trains": only trains running the telemetry command with cfg backbone_telemetry_enabled=True. On those, under cycles slower than snmp_telemetry_interval (slow/timing-out APs), telemetry to the NMS thins out as overrunning fires are skipped (graceful degradation, not crash/corruption; APScheduler logs a WARNING per skip but nothing is surfaced to the NMS consumer).

refuted.title: cfg["train_type"] bracket access raises KeyError and aborts report when train_type is unset
refuted.claim: Line 23 reads topology defensively with cfg.get('topology', {}), but line 34 accesses cfg['train_type'] via Configuration.__getitem__, which does Configuration._config[item] and raises KeyError if the key is missing. The multi-CCU branch (entered whenever box_coach_numbers is present in topology) therefore crashes CCUContext.__init__ for any train whose merged YAML config lacks train_type. Since CCUContext() is constructed at report time (report_generic.py:166, report.py:662), this aborts the entire report/validate run rather than degrading gracefully. The inconsistency with the defensive .get() one line earlier shows the guard was simply not applied here.
refuted.trigger: A train config that defines topology['box_coach_numbers'] but has no top-level train_type key (partial/misimaged config, or a config-merge gap).

verdict.reasoning:
The cited line is real in isolation: context.py:34 does `topology["box_coach_numbers"].get(cfg["train_type"], {})`, and `cfg["train_type"]` routes through Configuration.__getitem__ (configuration.py:108-109 `return Configuration._config[item]`), which raises KeyError on a missing key — while line 26 uses the defensive `if "ccu_box_id" in cfg:` and line 23 uses `cfg.get("topology", {})`. So the inconsistency the claim points to exists. BUT the claimed trigger is unreachable on the live path, for two independent reasons:

(1) Upstream guard. The only live construction of CCUContext() is GenericReport.get_current_ccu_box_and_coach (report_generic.py:166), reached only from GenericReport.number_coaches (line 67), which runs only inside run_report() (report.py:624). GenericReport.__init__ (report_generic.py:41-45) has a pre-flight check: `if self.train_type == "unknown": logger.critical(...); sys.exit(1)`. Since `self.train_type = self.cfg.get("train_type", "unknown")` (report.py:35), a merged config lacking train_type yields train_type=="unknown" and sys.exit(1) DURING __init__, before number_coaches/CCUContext is ever reached. A config that defines box_coach_numbers but omits train_type therefore cannot reach line 34 via GenericReport. The other construction site, Report.get_current_ccu_box_id (report.py:654/662), is dead code — never invoked anywhere in src (grep for get_current_ccu_box_id shows only its definition, no caller).

(2) Wrong blast radius for DOSTO. The trains this project concerns use DostoNeuReport (report_dosto_neu.py:30, `class DostoNeuReport(Report)` — NOT GenericReport). It overrides number_coaches() with its own neighbour-BFS and never constructs CCUContext nor reads box_coach_numbers. DOSTO reports cannot hit line 34 at all. The box_coach_numbers/CCUContext branch is used only by GenericReport and subclasses TGVReport/TGV2020Report (non-DOSTO), all behind the train_type guard.

So the KeyError is statically possible only if some future/other caller constructs CCUContext with box_coach_numbers-present-but-train_type-absent config bypassing the GenericReport guard; no such caller exists today. Claim's STATED BLAST ("all reports") is false and the central/high-blast-radius framing is incorrect — the line is on a non-DOSTO, guarded path.
verdict.covered_by_test: No covering test for the missing-train_type case. tests/lib/report/test_report_ccu2.py exercises the box_coach_numbers multi-CCU branch (topology-tgvm945-ccu2.yaml) but always sets configuration["train_type"] = name at line 49 before constructing GenericReport, so train_type is never absent. No test asserts the KeyError nor graceful degradation. The green test asserts correct coach numbering with train_type present (does not exercise the claimed failure mode).
verdict.blast_radius_adjusted: Not platform-wide and not applicable to DOSTO. The line is reachable only via GenericReport / TGVReport / TGV2020Report (non-DOSTO trains using the box_coach_numbers multi-CCU feature). DOSTO NEU trains use DostoNeuReport, which never constructs CCUContext or reads box_coach_numbers. Even for the GenericReport family, the missing-train_type trigger is pre-empted by the sys.exit(1) guard in GenericReport.__init__. Practically zero blast radius given the current caller set.

refuted.title: CCUContext is a never-refreshed process-global singleton; stale identity poisons every later report in serve_api
refuted.claim: _ccu_box_id and _ccu_coach_number are class attributes computed once under the _initialized guard (lines 18-53) and only ever cleared by reset() (documented 'for testing purposes'). In a long-running process, identity derived from a transient/wrong state at first construction (e.g. FQDN not yet resolvable at boot → socket.getfqdn() returns 'localhost' at line 29, or config reloaded later) is cached for the process lifetime and reused for every subsequent report. There is no production path to recompute it after the config or hostname becomes correct.
refuted.trigger: First CCUContext() construction occurs before FQDN/config is fully settled (boot race), or config is updated mid-process; all later reports keep the first (wrong) box id / coach number.

verdict.reasoning:
The code-level facts are accurate but the stated trigger and blast radius are wrong about the actual call graph, so the central claim as framed is refuted.

WHAT IS TRUE: context.py:18-53 caches _ccu_box_id/_ccu_coach_number as class attributes once under the _initialized guard, cleared only by reset() (documented 'for testing purposes', line 67). socket.getfqdn() (line 29) is used only when topology has 'box_coach_numbers' AND config lacks 'ccu_box_id'. There is no production recompute path.

WHY IT IS REFUTED:
1. serve_api does NOT generate reports. obn.py:136-153 (serve_api) runs uvicorn over lib/server, whose routers (server/routers/consist.py, actions.py) only call cli.update.load_report(cfg.report_file) — they read the report JSON from disk. Grep confirms the ONLY callers of CCUContext() are lib/report/report.py:662 and lib/report/report_generic.py:166, both reached via Report.run_report(). run_report() is invoked solely by the one-shot CLI command 'obn report' (obn.py:76-90: instantiates reporter, calls run_report(), process exits). So 'poisons every later report in serve_api' describes a path that does not exist — serve_api produces no reports via CCUContext, and the report producer is not a long-running process.
2. Because each 'obn report' is a fresh process, CCUContext is constructed exactly once per process from fresh config; there is no process-lifetime reuse across multiple reports to be poisoned.
3. The FQDN boot-race sub-scenario is narrower still: for DOSTO-NEU single-CCU trains 'box_coach_numbers' is typically absent, so the else branch (lines 47-52) runs, hardcoding 'box1' and reading box1_coach_number from config — socket.getfqdn() is never called. getfqdn() only matters for multi-CCU trains with box_coach_numbers set and no ccu_box_id in config.
4. 'config reloaded later mid-process' is not a real path: Configuration is itself a process-global singleton (configuration.py:45-46 returns early if _config already set), so config does not reload within a process for either class.

The staleness mechanism exists in the abstract, but the TITLE ('poisons every later report in serve_api'), TRIGGER (long-running serve_api with config/FQDN settling later), and STATED BLAST ('all reports') are all false against this codebase's actual call graph.
verdict.covered_by_test: No test covers the staleness/blast-radius claim. tests/conftest.py:11 calls CCUContext.reset() in the teardown of the 'configuration' fixture — this is the standard singleton-reset-between-tests pattern, not an assertion about staleness in either direction. No test in tests/lib/report exercises a long-running process reusing a stale CCUContext, and none asserts the bug or the opposite.
verdict.blast_radius_adjusted: Not platform-wide as stated. The cache is consumed only by Report.run_report() via report.py:662 / report_generic.py:166, which runs in the one-shot 'obn report' CLI process (obn.py:76-90) — a fresh process per invocation that builds the context once from fresh config. serve_api (the long-running process named in the claim) never touches CCUContext; its routers read the report file from disk. The getfqdn boot-race only applies to multi-CCU trains with topology.box_coach_numbers set and no ccu_box_id in config; single-CCU DOSTO-NEU trains take the box1 else-branch and never call getfqdn. Effective blast radius: theoretical, confined to multi-CCU report runs where FQDN is unresolved at the exact moment of the single per-process construction.

refuted.title: CCUDevice.mac caches the 'unknown' sentinel for the whole process on ioctl failure
refuted.claim: mac is a cached_property: on a virtual CCU or transient ioctl failure it returns 'unknown' (line 53), which the cached_property then stores in obj.__dict__ and returns for the rest of the process with no retry. Where the CCU's own MAC is used as an identity/cache key or report field, it is pinned to 'unknown'. Lower blast radius than the context findings because it is the CCU's own MAC and only memory-cached per process, but it is a cache-a-failure pattern in identity code.
refuted.trigger: ioctl SIOCETHTOOL fails or is unavailable (virtual CCU, missing lan0/lan1) on first access to .mac.

verdict.reasoning: The mechanical core of the claim is statically true: CCUDevice.mac (ccudevice.py:26-56) is decorated with lib.util.decorators.cached_property, whose __get__ (decorators.py:33-37) stores the returned value — including the "unknown" sentinel from line 53 — into obj.__dict__ and returns it for the rest of the process with no retry. However the claim is REFUTED as a fault because the behavior is (a) explicitly intentional and documented, and (b) covered by green tests asserting exactly this. Lines 42-44 carry a code comment: "If the ioctl call fails (e.g. on a virtual CCU), the OSError is suppressed and the info value will stay on -1, triggering a warning." The return of "unknown" is the designed graceful-degradation contract, not an accident. The OSError is caught via contextlib.suppress(OSError) (line 48) — there IS an upstream guard. The "no retry" objection is hollow: "unknown" only arises when the lan0/lan1 ethtool ioctl is persistently unavailable (virtual CCU / missing interface), a condition that does not heal mid-process, so a retry would re-yield "unknown"; caching changes nothing observable. Caller impact is benign and degrades gracefully: walker.py:73 adds the value to a dedup set found_mac_addresses (real device MACs are hex strings from SNMP/LLDP — no harmful collision with "unknown"); tng4500.py:176 evaluates "unknown".startswith("00:14:5a") -> False, falling through to the ARP lookup path; report_queensland.py:44 already initialises master_ccu_mac = "unknown" by default and is a non-DOSTO project. No DOSTO discovery/report path uses ccu.mac as a load-bearing identity key that would silently emit wrong output. The stated blast radius ("one device") is already minimal and the realistic operational impact is essentially none on real hardware (ioctl succeeds, real MAC caches).
verdict.covered_by_test: tests/lib/device/test_ccudevice.py — test_mac__failed_ioctl (line 49: assert ccu.mac == "unknown") and test_mac__ioctl_exception (line 58: assert ccu.mac == "unknown") both green-assert the exact "unknown" fallback, confirming it is intended contract. test_mac (line 40) covers the success path. No test asserts caching/retry, but the fallback value is the asserted behavior.
verdict.blast_radius_adjusted: One device (the CCU's own MAC), and only on virtual/ioctl-unavailable CCUs. On real hardware the ioctl succeeds and the real MAC caches. Callers (walker dedup set, tng4500 startswith->ARP fallback, queensland default) all degrade gracefully with no silent wrong output on DOSTO paths. Effectively no operational blast radius.

refuted.title: NomadCCUEngineManager shares one global SnmpEngine with no lock across telemetry threads
refuted.claim: snmp_engine is a class-level singleton instantiated once (lines 22-27) and reused throughout the run; neighbours() (lines 60-107) calls getCmd directly against self.snmp_engine. A single pysnmp SnmpEngine carries mutable dispatcher/cache state and is not safe to share concurrently. If the telemetry scheduler ever fans CCU SNMP queries across threads, the shared engine is used without any lock, risking interleaved dispatcher state. The vendor comment 'reuse the same SnmpEngine instance throughout the application's run' shows reuse is intentional but thread-safety is unaddressed.
refuted.trigger: Concurrent SNMP queries through the shared NomadCCU SnmpEngine from multiple telemetry/scheduler threads.

verdict.reasoning: The static facts in the claim are correct: NomadCCUEngineManager.snmp_engine is a class-level singleton (nomad_ccu.py:22-27) and neighbours() calls getCmd directly against self.snmp_engine with no lock (nomad_ccu.py:60-107). But the claim is refuted on its stated trigger and overstated on blast radius. (1) The exact trigger named -- "telemetry scheduler fans CCU SNMP queries across threads" -- is directly contradicted by the code: backbone_telemetry.py:94-101 says "Previous versions of OBN telemetry made use of a ThreadPoolExecutor ... but this didn't play well with the new singleton SNMP engine manager. With the engine manager and no threads ..." and the current telemetry() is a plain sequential loop (`for device in device_instances: telemetry_device(device)`). The maintainers already removed the threading on the engine path on purpose. (2) The ONLY real concurrency in the tree is cli/update.py:324-327 process_batch -> ThreadPoolExecutor -> update_device, and that path acts on switch/AP vendor devices via get_snmpdevice (update.py:143-144) which use the SEPARATE SNMPEngineManager singleton, not NomadCCUEngineManager. The cited neighbours() method is invoked only from single-threaded walkers (lldpwalker.py:30-41 sequential while-loop; dhcpwalker; lldparpwalker) and report modules -- never from the threaded batch. The CCU device/engine cited has no concurrent caller in this codebase. The generic pysnmp-engine-shared-across-threads concern is real in principle, but as framed (NomadCCU engine + telemetry threads) the trigger does not occur; the genuine residual exposure is on a different singleton (SNMPEngineManager) and a different module (update.process_batch), not the cited finding.
verdict.covered_by_test: Partially. tests/lib/device/vendor/test_nomad_ccu.py exercises neighbours() with mocked getCmd (test_handle, test_handle_dual) but only single-threaded and asserts nothing about engine sharing or concurrency. tests/cli/test_update.py mocks out process_batch entirely (line 576: mocker.patch("cli.update.process_batch")), so the ThreadPoolExecutor + shared-engine interaction is never executed by any test. No test asserts the race exists, and none asserts thread-safety either.
verdict.blast_radius_adjusted: Narrower than "all SNMP devices." As cited (NomadCCUEngineManager + CCU neighbours()), there is no concurrent caller, so the practical blast radius of the stated finding is effectively nil. The only theoretical concurrent-shared-engine path is SNMPEngineManager driving switch/AP firmware/config pushes in cli/update.process_batch -- a different singleton and module from the one cited -- and even that is bounded to the small per-batch device set during a supervised `obn update` run, not platform-wide telemetry.
